note: Two statements only: amounts relative to the repository, a frozen text encoder. Nothing on what keeps later content out, on structure features or on cost.

Typed nodes; content as chunk nodes from a frozen encoder; events carry exact 1/n and decay products; amounts as quantiles of the repository's own past; return probabilities, no eigenvectors. Open: the number of chunk nodes and content hashes is not counted. A frozen encoder cannot learn a repository's own words.

Exact aggregates per pair plus a fine-tuned encoder reading question and file together. The aggregates are the same mechanism as A1.c.1 with fewer of them; the joint reading is A2's matter. Transfer of the tuned encoder rests on a test; a pattern outside the bank is lost (D 9.2).

Words as nodes, no pretrained part: a lexical score becomes a two-step sum, and no encoder cut-off binds the test date. Reach only through shared subwords; word vectors trained on the training repositories; the size of the term graph is not counted.

A tuned code model reads text; events and links as typed soft tokens; raw amounts go round the model so sums stay exact; closed-walk counts and return probabilities. Open, each with its named test: transfer of the tuned weights, what the pretrained model already read of later public history, and the cost of a tuned pass per candidate.

Text enters only as relevance amounts from frozen models. Same mechanism as the text columns of A1.c.1. It cannot learn what relevance means for this task, and the record shows untuned text models swinging by repository.

Exact sums over typed paths of at most two links, symbol and text matches, every amount relative to the question's candidates and the repository. Cheap and exact. Its limit is D 9.2: a pattern not listed is lost before learning, and text meets code only through numbers.

The raw relational graph with symbol nodes, root marks and an encoder trained further. Same mechanism as A1.a.1 with a trained encoder in place of a frozen one, which adds an open point on transfer. Its symbol nodes are not in A1.a.1.

Exact facts written as text for a cross-encoder. The count reaches the score only as written tokens, so its effect is learned and need not be exact. Its rule for choosing which part of a file is read (the definitions of names the question uses) is exact and not in the other thoughts.
Names two mechanisms without their form: every node described from the question as anchor, and attention between question and a retrieved set. Each is stated exactly elsewhere (A2.a.1, A2.a.3).

The question is a node; its starting files are marked by kind; every candidate also has an edge from the question carrying a joint reading of question and content; sums propagate from there; a fixed read-out. Relative to the question for all three questions, also where the question names no file. Open: one joint reading per candidate and one propagation per question.

An exact record per question and candidate: every typed path of at most two links, enumerated in full, with counts and decayed size-weighted sums, plus a joint reading of the text. Sees nothing past two links; its relational block is empty when the question names no file.

Attention among the question and the retrieved candidates with a relational term in the attention score; candidates are also described relative to each other. Counts reach a candidate's score only through a normalised attention weight, so the exact count is not a function of this form alone.

One encoder reads question and candidate as one sequence, with a relation token per kind of link built from the exact amounts, and a linear term that carries the exact amounts past the encoder. Open: transfer of the trained reader, what it read in pretraining, one pass per pair.

Marked starting files and typed sums over the whole graph; every file alive gets a rank at the cost of a few sparse passes. For task words the text meets a file's content only as one similarity of two vectors computed apart, so on the text side the description is relative to the question only in part.

Same mechanism as A2.a.2 (an exact relational profile read by a ranker). Its text side rests on a lexical score and one similarity of two vectors computed apart. Its soft starting files for task words and its typed distance are not in A2.a.2.

Same mechanism as A2.a.1 (propagation from marked starting files). The question's text reaches a candidate only through the starting files and a final pairing of two vectors; where the question names no file nothing marks the graph.

Same mechanism as A2.b.1 (question and candidate read jointly), with the relational facts written in words. Numbers in words are read approximately, so the count depends on the numbers also reaching the ranker directly.
A gated sum over change nodes that holds the exact count, with exact encodings over the whole history. Silent on the asking time; sampling 'by importance' has no stated design.

Two sum steps through event nodes per starting file, with trainable decay and size scalars and a bounded gate; activity channels separate a real link from a file that changes often; sum and max over starting files. Events are weighed only by kind and flags; nothing is designed for very large events.

A fixed grid of decayed, size-weighted statistics computed by the loader. Exact on the grid; a decay between grid points is approximated, on the test the thought names. One clock, no order, no second step.

The sum through event nodes with a bounded, unnormalised gate per event that depends on the question and on what the event was; the neutral gate is the exact count. The only thought that makes history relative to the question's content. Open: the gate may learn one repository's message habits; a stored vector per event.

The exact kernel sums of A3.c.1 given to a language model as tokens, with a linear path to the score, plus the text of the heaviest events. The sums are the same mechanism as A3.c.1; the text list is a short view of the history beside them.
A learned message per event, summed, one output fixed to the exact count. Same mechanism as A3.c.2 without a design for pairs with very many events.

An exact bank of size-weighted, decayed sums on two clocks in the repository's own units, with rates in both directions, order-restricted sums and two-step sums; a learned mix. Cannot weigh an event by what it is; nothing outside the bank.

A learned sum over joint events as nodes, with a fixed channel that always holds the exact count over all events; where a pair has very many events the learned part is summed over a sample drawn with known probabilities and reweighted. Open: joint events per pair.
A message function per kind and direction. Nothing bounds the parameters as kinds are added (N 13.2).

Each kind once per direction, all sharing a few base matrices, sums without division, a gate from the edge's own amounts; each relation pattern of N 13.8 is argued. Open: sampling at hubs; an unnormalised sum at a file with thousands of links needs relative amounts.
Exact counts of typed paths, a learned weight per path type. Same mechanism as A4.c.1; a path through a hub counts like any other, and the number of types is left to a bound still to be counted.

Typed, directed paths written as statements for a cross-encoder, grouped by signature, the group size entering through a numeric adapter. No parameters per kind; a new or rare kind is a phrase. Open on the test it names: that the model reads direction from word order.
Same mechanism as A4.a.1 (relational sums with shared bases, both directions), without the gate on an edge's amounts and without the scale problem named.

Kind and direction as a term in the attention score of every head, over a retrieved set read as one sequence. The softmax loses counts, and a pair with no link is described by one shortest path of many.

At most 468 typed path types of one and two links from the starting files: raw sums, sums discounted by the degree of the middle file, and the number of starting files that reach the candidate. Every relation pattern is representable because nothing is embedded. Blind past two links and to which symbol a link carries.
Same mechanism as A4.a.1. It gives the degree per kind as an input so hub size stays visible, and leaves the exact count open on a test.
An embedding of the age at the asking time. Nothing keeps the exact decayed count, and nothing is said on what keeps later facts out.

Ages on the repository's own clocks, a fixed bank of decays with a learned mix per kind of link inside summed messages, three locks against later facts, no state kept between questions. Cannot represent a decay that is not monotone.
One replay in time order keeps exact traces per pair. Same mechanism as A5.c.1 on one clock, without its activity and order columns; memory per pair not counted.

Relative clocks, the exact decay bank given to the language model as one token, recent events as ordered text. It alone names the second leak: a pretrained model's own cut-off must come before the validation stretch, and every example is marked by it. Open on the count it names.
A learned time function inside summed messages, the fixed decays kept; the text model holds no time. Same mechanism as the kept A3.c.2. Exact only in expectation where events are sampled.

One access path to the facts visible before the asking time; two clocks in the repository's scale; an exact bank of decays with a learned mix; the candidate's own activity; directed order counts. Auditable by the data design's own leak test. Cannot represent a decay that is not monotone.
Same mechanism as A5.b.2 and the kept A3.c.2. The learned part has no constraint at ages longer than any seen in training (the limit of D 8.1 for a network).

The decay curve is counted from the repository's own past at the asking time and pulled towards a curve from the training repositories when the history is short. Nothing per repository is learned, and shapes that are not monotone are covered. Weak on short histories; mixes coupling with a file that changes often unless that rate is given beside it.

dropped.reason: Contained in A1.a.1, which says the same two things and what keeps later content out, the structure features and the events.
Same mechanism as A1.c.1 for the exact aggregates, with fewer of them; its joint reading of text belongs to A2 and is kept there (A2.a.2).
Reach only through shared subwords, weaker on M6 than a pretrained encoder; its exact lexical score is a column of A1.c.1. Its one advantage, no encoder cut-off, is noted.
Same mechanism as the text columns of A1.c.1 (text as relevance amounts from frozen models); cannot learn what relevance means for the task.
Same mechanism as A1.a.1 with an encoder trained further, which adds an open point on transfer (M3). Its symbol nodes are not in A1.a.1.
M2 in part: the count reaches the score only as written tokens. A1.b.1 serves the same reader with the amounts kept exact beside it.
Names two mechanisms without their form; A2.a.1 states the first exactly, A2.a.3 the second.

M2 in part: counts reach a candidate's score only through a normalised attention weight (N 9.5, N 12.6). Three other mechanisms are kept, the limit of the plan. What it adds, candidates described relative to each other, is a matter of the scoring form (A7).

Same mechanism as A2.a.1; on the text side M1 only in part (one similarity of two vectors computed apart, N 9.8), where A2.a.1 reads question and content jointly. Its rank for every file alive at the cost of sparse passes is noted for A6.
Same mechanism as A2.a.2; on the text side M1 only in part (N 9.8). Its soft starting files for task words are not in A2.a.2.
Same mechanism as A2.a.1; M1 only in part: where the question names no file nothing marks the graph, and the text reaches a candidate only through a final pairing of two vectors.
Same mechanism as A2.b.1 with the facts in words: M2 in part, where A2.b.1 carries the exact amounts on a linear path.
Contained in A3.c.1 and A3.c.2, which also say what keeps later facts out and how very many events are sampled.
Same mechanism as A3.c.2 (a learned sum through event nodes); weighs an event only by kind and flags and has no design for pairs with very many events.
Same mechanism as A3.c.1 with fewer statistics: one clock, no order, no second step; exact only on its grid (M2 open).

Its sums are the mechanism of A3.c.1; its text list of the heaviest events is a short view beside them. Weighing events by what they were about, relative to the question, is done without losing counts by A3.a.3.
Same mechanism as A3.c.2 without the sampling design for very many events (M7 open with no way named).
Contained in A4.a.1, which bounds the parameters by shared bases (N 13.2).
Same mechanism as A4.c.1, which also discounts paths through hubs and fixes the number of path types.
Same mechanism as A4.a.1 without the gate on an edge's own amounts.
M2 in part: the softmax loses counts, and a pair with no link is described by one shortest path of many (N 9.5, N 12.6).
Same mechanism as A4.a.1 with the exact count left open on a test. Its degree-per-kind input for hubs is not in A4.a.1.
An age embedding alone: M2 and M4 in part. Contained in A5.c.1 and A3.c.2.
Same mechanism as A5.c.1 (a fixed bank of decays on the repository's clocks, the mix learned), placed inside messages; its three locks give the same guarantee as A5.c.1's single access path.
Same mechanism as A5.c.1 computed by replay, on one clock and without the activity and order columns.
A learned time function inside summed messages with the fixed decays kept: the mechanism of the kept A3.c.2. M2 exact only in expectation where events are sampled.
Same as A5.b.2; M3 open: the learned part has no constraint at ages beyond those seen in training (D 8.1).

note: Names retrieval and attention for far reach and a depth, without their form: nothing on which candidates the scorer sees, how every file alive gets a rank, or the cost.

Restart walks from the question node per relation group with the degree bias removed, content edges from the question to every file, a first-stage ranker for every file, the top set scored by the rooted model over a direct edge. Reach by any path length or by content, every file ranked, on processors. A right file outside the candidate set keeps only its first-stage rank; that recall is a count for the cards.

Far files by content alone (token-level matching under a tuned encoder, exact symbols, text search); structure only within two hops. M6 in part: a right file tied only by a route of three or more links and sharing no content is outside the mechanism. M7 open on the storage of a token-level index; M3 open on whether a tuned encoder carries to unseen repositories (the record shows retrievers swinging by repository).

A probability for every file alive by descent of the folder tree, each folder scored relative to the question from exact sums over its files; no candidate cut; a file with no signal of its own inherits its folder's. Linear in the number of nodes. M6 open on its named count: whether right files cluster in folders that carry a signal. A low score high up lowers everything below; nothing gained in a flat repository.

Every file scored by a linear mix of channels (frozen chunk similarity with a tuned question side, text search, identifiers the decoder proposes and that must resolve in the symbol table, exact history and two-hop counts); the top set read jointly. M6 in part: reach is by content and names; structure stops at two hops. M7 open on chunks per repository. M4 open: a proposed name may be recalled from the decoder's training, which its own test (repositories created before and after the cut-off) reads.

Exact restart walks over typed graphs that include content-neighbour edges among files, bias removed by the stationary visit. M1 in part: the question enters only through seeds (its files, or text-search hits), not through its meaning; a wrong seed is amplified. M6 open on its count; M7 open on the cost of the neighbour graph per tree.

The decoder walks down the folder tree, reading the question together with each listing whose children carry exact subtree sums; a probability per file; training needs no sampled negatives. M7 open: one language-model pass per folder on the path, listing length uncounted. M6 open: rests on names describing content, and a beam that drops a folder leaves its files a coarse rank. M4 open as for any decoder that reads names.

For every file alive: restart-walk mass from the question's files per relation group and restart rate, the same over stationary mass, hop distance to the start set, an echo through similar past units of work, and content matches. A ranker scores every file and a new-file entry per folder; the reader rescores the top set. Reach by a path of any length, a word, a name or a similar past unit; computed, not learned; O(E) per product. The order of kinds along a route is lost in the pooled group.

Folder tokens built by sums, read together with the question by one attention biased by exact counts between folders; a summed score, so a wrong folder lowers a file and never removes it. M3 open: attention learned over layout conventions may not carry to an unseen repository. M7 open on folders per repository; above a stated number it attends one level up first, which brings a cut back. Large folders over-load their token.

Names three properties (a ranking loss over the list, negatives by a known design, weights) without the form: nothing on several right files, on a new file, on what the model outputs or on how examples are weighted.

Each right file against wrong files only; neighbourhood negatives scored whole, far ones drawn with known probabilities and corrected; an exact-count term with non-negative weight, so the class contains decayed counting; virtual slot nodes per folder for a new file; one-over-number-of-right-files inside a question. The log of the estimated sum is biased low and the bias shrinks with the number of draws (stated). A folder not yet made has no slot.

A tree ranker over the exact pair record, pairs weighted by how much a swap changes the reading measure, ranks among all files estimated from draws with known probabilities. Amounts relative, so not under W10. It cannot pass a gradient to an encoder, and a right file far down the list gets almost no pull although the data design also reads every rank.

A probability per file: a sigmoid with a base-rate offset computed from the repository's own past, a weighted cross-entropy that is an unbiased estimate of the full loss. It can say how many files are right. M7 open: fitted on probability, not on order, with the easy wrong files dominating and a high variance where draw probabilities are small; whether it orders the top as well as a listwise loss is a test.

The same listwise form on the cross-encoder's logit: a fixed set of hard files plus draws from a known mix, every right file of the same unit of work kept out of the negatives, a list of their own for new-file slots. M7 open on its own count: tuned passes per question times questions against three cards for eight hours.

A measure-weighted tree ranker in which the language-model score is one column, fitted on the other half of the training repositories so the ranker meets it as it will be on unseen ones. M7 open: each stage sees half the repositories, and whether half suffices is uncounted. M1 in part: text meets counts only through splits on one score.

A calibrated probability with the base rate following only the number of files through a learned coefficient: M3 in part, since the repository's own habits (how many files a change has) are not read. M7 open as for A7.a.3.

Score = the baseline of the kind of question as a fixed offset plus a learned part; candidates are every file alive plus a slot per folder with features of its own; each right file against wrong files only; every candidate with a relational feature taken whole, the rest by Poisson sampling with known probabilities, reweighted; equal weight per repository with a bound. With the learned part at zero it is the baseline on the same examples. Bias of the log stated; an unlabelled right file is label noise, not a drawn right answer.

A joint reader as a residual on a frozen first score, inside a retrieved set; negatives drawn from the files the first score confuses, with known probability; pairs weighted by the change in the top ten. M7 open: the loss is conditional on the retrieved set and its swap weight is computed on the sample, so its expectation is no known total; pairs per hour uncounted.

A probability per file from a Bernoulli likelihood estimated as an unbiased total: every related candidate whole, the rest by Poisson sampling; an offset that is an exact statistic of the repository before the asking time, plus the baseline of the kind of question. Says how many files to show. M7 open on its own test: whether its ranks fall below the listwise form's. Right files that come together are scored as independent trials.

One shared model with an encoder per kind of question, marked as an assumption. An encoder of its own leaves the error question to train from few examples; nothing on what else is shared, on stages or on how training mixes the questions.

One rooted network for all three questions: the kind is an input, a kind owns only its mixing numbers in the shared relation basis, the error question fits only those; retrieve and rank are the same model run twice with the joint reader masked in the first pass; every step mixes all kinds. M7 open on what every design with a reader shares: propagations and joint readings per question against three cards for eight hours (A9). A kind cannot get a direction outside the span of the bases; negative transfer is its own test.

Shared exact features, one shared joint reader, a base ranker pooled over kinds and a boosted residual per kind with strong shrinkage; retrieval a separate untrained union. A regularity learned on one kind reaches another only through the base ranker's splits. M7 open on the reader's pairs.

Every question is first turned into weighted starting files (a change: its files; an error: trace files weighted by a monotone curve of frame depth; task words: named files plus the top text-search hits with normalised weights); one shared scorer, linear in the seeds, so counts from each seed stay exact. The error question fits only the depth curve. A right file tied to no seed rests on the reader alone; a wrong search hit pulls in its partners.

Specialists by kind of evidence (history, structure, a joint text reader), each with its own ranking loss, and a combiner per kind of question fitted on scores from fits that did not see the example; the error combiner is the change combiner plus a correction pulled to zero. M7 open: every specialist is fitted on half of the training clusters. The combiner sees scalars, so evidence that must be bound below it is lost (a projection).

One relational model trained end to end, everything shared except a mark per starting kind and a kind token; candidates from an untrained union of exact channels; kinds drawn in proportion to the square root of their counts. The same mechanism as A8.a.1. M7 open: one propagation per question.

The score is a sum of stages, each trained with the earlier ones frozen as an offset: the untrained baseline of the kind of question, a ranker on exact pair features, a joint reader over the top set; the offsets the reader trains on come from fits that did not see the example. The exact count is the first stage itself; the reader's gradient falls where the cheaper stages misrank; each stage's gain is read apart. A stage cannot be retrained alone, and a file below the cut never reaches the reader. M7 open on pairs per question.

One backbone for the three questions and a small part per kind of question (on the exact linear term, on the read-out, a low-rank adapter on the reader), each pulled toward zero so a kind with little data falls back on the shared head; the linear exact term ranks every file, the backbone re-ranks the top set; one run, all kinds in every batch, each kind's loss normalised. It contains the fully shared form as its limit. A head cannot restore what the backbone never computes. M7 open on the reader's pairs (A9).

A separate ranker per question with data, sharing nothing learned; the error question composed from both by a few weights fitted on scores from fits that left out the example's cluster. No kind can pull another down, and each ranker may take the form that suits its question. It gives up what sharing teaches (the task-words reader learns from its own questions only), and a conjunction across the two scores is lost to a linear stacker.

A6.c.1 adds the hop distance, the echo through similar past units and the new-file entries. Not in A6.c.1: the candidate set as the union of each channel's top files.

Same mechanism as A6.b.1 (reach by content, structure only within two hops), with M7 open on the storage of a token-level index and M3 open on a tuned encoder's transfer. Its token-level matching is not in A6.b.1.

Same route as A6.a.3 (the folder tree as the hierarchy) by a learned attention over folder tokens: M3 open (layout conventions may not carry over, N 8.4) and M7 open; above a stated number of folders it brings a cut back.

Same mechanism as A7.c.3 (a calibrated probability, an unbiased weighted cross-entropy, a base rate computed from the repository's own past). A7.c.3 takes the related candidates whole, which lowers the variance A7.a.3 names.
Same mechanism as A7.c.3; M3 in part: its base rate follows only the number of files, through a learned coefficient.

An encoder per kind of question leaves the error question to train its own from few examples (D 7.4); nothing on stages or on how training mixes the questions.

Same mechanism as A8.c.1 (a pooled base and a residual per kind pulled to zero) in trees; a regularity learned on one kind reaches another only through the base ranker's splits.

why: Every run-written thought of A8 is at the same levels on the profiles the part bears on (M1 and M3 by construction, M7 open on the count of joint readings, which belongs to A9), so the order is in words. Three ways of serving the three questions are kept, one per mechanism: one shared model with a small part per question (A8.c.1), a separate ranker per question (A8.c.2), parts by kind of evidence trained in stages (A8.b.3).

note: Exact columns for every file (decay bank on two clocks, typed counts, restart walks, echo, text), a linear first stage with the counting baseline as offset, then a three-layer question-rooted propagation over the top set with sums, 28 relations on shared bases and per-event gates whose neutral point is the exact count; one backbone with small parts per question. Every veto read: nearest W1 (not met: marks, exact columns and name matches are pair computations) and W5 (reach is computed, three layers). Lacks, in words. Content: a file's text is read only through vectors of a frozen encoder computed without the question, also inside the top set, where its own parent A2.a.1 asks for a joint reading; a repository's private vocabulary is out of reach. M4: nothing keeps the encoder's cut-off before the validation stretch and examples are not marked. M3: the propagation's sums are bounded by a logarithm, not put on the repository's own scale. A decay that is not monotone only inside the top set. The top set always ranks above the rest. M7 open on tokens for the frozen pass, edges per repository against 96 GB, recall at K.

A cascade: the counted baseline, a small network over exact features and text channels for every file, then a tuned code decoder reading question and shortlisted file together with relation tokens, a history token and the latest events; the stricter cut-off rule with marked examples. Every veto read: nearest W1 (outside the shortlist the dense channel is two vectors, beside pair-specific channels) and W4 (the event list is short, the bank covers all history). M6 in part: far files are reached by content and by names the decoder proposes; structure stops at two hops, and a right file tied only by a longer route or by a similar past unit of work has no channel. Other lacks: decay monotone only; nothing per question beyond the offset; the shortlist always above the rest; the causal reading is argued from N 12.6, which speaks of the complete graph. M7 open: time binds (about 90,000 questions at 1.5 billion parameters argued), throughput and distinct content uncounted.

Everything exact is computed for every file alive (kernel bank on two clocks, 468 typed path types, a lag curve counted per repository, reach by any path, echo, text); the score is the baseline plus boosted trees over that record plus, in a shortlist, a tuned joint reader whose head also reads the exact record; stages trained on offsets from fits that did not see the example; one score ranks every file. Every veto read: nearest W10 (trees, on relative amounts only) and W1 (the cosine channel, never alone). Lacks, in words. An event is weighed by size and age only, never by what it was or by the question. Nothing is per question except the offset and the start kind; the error question has no part of its own. M4: the reader's cut-off rule is the data design's only; nothing keeps it before the validation stretch. Typed composition stops at two links. Outside the shortlist text meaning rests on vectors computed apart. M7 open on rows per question, processor hours for the record, pairs per hour, and on whether a reader of a few hundred million parameters is what the compute allows or only an assumption.

A linear first stage over cheap channels for every file, then a two-layer question-rooted propagation over the shortlist in which each candidate's input is the tuned decoder's joint reading of question and file, with per-event gates and ungated exact columns kept beside them; small parts per question; the stricter cut-off rule; shortlists from fits on the other half of the clusters. Every veto read: nearest W1 and W5, neither met. M6 in part, as C2: reach by content and proposed names, structure to two hops, no channel for a longer route or a similar past unit. Other lacks: decay monotone only; a file in the shortlist always above one outside. M7 open and the tightest of the four by its own count: the decoder's frozen pass over all content takes about 7 of 24 card-hours at half a billion parameters and too much above that, so the reader's size is held down by the vectors.

dropped.reason: M6 in part: its reach to far files is by content and by names the decoder proposes; structure stops at two hops, and a right file tied only by a longer structural route or by a similar past unit of work has no channel.
